intro: Reaching a server, signing in on each kind of device, keeping several accounts on one.
What is around every screen: the rail or tab bar, the top bar, going back.
The first screen: the hero and the rows.
Every movie and every show, filtered and sorted.
A movie's or a show's page: what it is, its seasons and episodes, its extras, what can be done with it.
Cast and crew: a person's page and what they were in.
What a person keeps to watch, in lists of their own, and what they watched.
Finding a title or a person by name.
Titles one after the other, playing from their middle, to find something to watch.
Playing a title: resume, quality, audio, skipping, the next episode, the picture.
Choosing subtitles and how they look, in every kind of subtitle the library holds.
Keeping a title on a phone to watch without a connection.
Playing on a TV from a phone or a computer.
What the server tells a person, in the bell.
A person's settings, reporting a problem, and the account itself.
Where everyone signs in: the spaces, their tiles, the search across them, an app opened in place.
What the home page shows and where: the registry admins edit.
Adding, installing, setting up and removing addons, and what an addon may add to the platform.
Who may use the platform: people, their roles, invites.
Keeping it running: its parts, updates, checks, logs, events, its database, a support bundle, the first-run checklist.
What the library holds, as the catalog knows it: scanning, details, metadata, the rules a title must meet.
The packages the apps play, and the originals they were made from: verified, then retired.
What happens to a new title: analysed, encoded, packaged, given subtitles; and encoding while it plays.
The platform as an operator installs it: identity, storage, addresses, certificates, backups, updates.
A product for live channels: registered, not built.
A product for music: registered, not built.
Listening and reading: expected, neither registered nor built.
